exposure: Etiology of thrombocytopenia (preeclampsia, preeclampsia with HELLP syndrome, gestational, infectious)
outcome: Fetomaternal complications (antepartum hemorrhage, postpartum hemorrhage, ICU admission, mortality, neonatal ICU admission)
cohort: 150 pregnant patients admitted to labor ward with thrombocytopenia at a tertiary care teaching public hospital over 1 year
finding: Preeclampsia with or without HELLP syndrome and vector-borne infections such as malaria, dengue, and leptospirosis were found to be very important causes of moderate to severe thrombocytopenia and were associated with complications.
